'''DeckTech''' (decktech.net) was a major SWCCG deck-list and tournament-report site in the late 1990s–2000s. The [[Players Committee]] later wrote that PC forums slowly overtook DeckTech, [[Game Players Network]], and other sites as the primary online hangout.<ref name="pc-net">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community-network/ Community Network], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20170709120918/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community-network/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Stephen Skilton's [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/ SWCCG Decktech Archives] keep 3,923 Star Wars deck posts (ids 3–26555, 11 August 1999 through 10 December 2002) and 1,406 tournament-report URLs. A GitHub Pages copy of the same dump is at [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/ stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives]. This wiki dests those posts onto [[DeckTech decks]] and [[DeckTech tournament reports]]; the Skilton hosts stay in Sources.

The same 3,923 posts are also hosted at [http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/decks/ decktech.net]; individual posts are at `/starwarsccg/deck/{id}`. Title, author, handle, side, and rating letter indexes on that host 404. Listing Light/Dark tags on the archive index are often wrong (a Hunt Down post tagged Light).

Tournament reports name pairings, finishes, and sometimes include a 60. Dest those reports as articles and use them to fill event hubs and player Tournament Results.

DeckTech ran the [[FreedomCon]] charity convention in Virginia Beach on 15&ndash;18 November 2001; its Star Wars CCG tournament is counted as the [[2001 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="fc-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon home page], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011201221615/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 1 December 2001]</ref> After Decipher lost the Star Wars license, DeckTech ran a second FreedomCon, in Lansdale, Pennsylvania, on 4&ndash;6 October 2002, organized by [[Michael Carr|Mike Carr]].<ref name="fc2-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon Philadelphia 2002 home page], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030112115941/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 12 January 2003]</ref>

== DeckTech Player's Challenge and Premium Membership ==

On 13 December 2002 the [[Players Committee]] announced an "exclusive and strategic partnership" with Decktech Inc., which it called "the best CCG resource on the Internet"; their co-sponsored DPC Championship Series would let players qualify for Worlds and win cash, "taking the first pro series for SWCCG (DPCs) to a new level".<ref name="pcf-428-6399">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=6399#6399 Player's Committee Outlines Road to Worlds 2003], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 December 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040318153243/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=6642%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In May 2003, as deck discussion left Decipher's boards, [[Nick Kolnik]] said deck submissions and reviews should go through the Committee's partner sites DeckTech and [[Game Players Network]].<ref name="pcf-1448-25382">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=25382#25382 following on from what GO was saying...], Nick Kolnik, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 May 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041120152757/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=25407%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> The first DeckTech Player's Challenge (DPC) was held in Normal, Illinois, and drew more than 80 players.<ref name="pc-dpcchicago03">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/dpcchicago.htm DPC Goes Back to it's Roots; Next Stop is the Windy City!], swccgpc.com (2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040604153526/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/dpcchicago.htm Internet Archive]</ref> DeckTech, Inc. and the [[Players Committee]] co-sponsored [[2003 DPC Chicago|DPC Chicago]], held at Pastimes in Niles, Illinois, on 11–13 April 2003; its DPC Championship was the kickoff of the Committee's new professional tournament series.<ref name="pc-dpcchicago03" /> The series also had a DPC Championship at [[2003 Origins|Origins 2003]].<ref name="pc-premium0612">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/originspremium06122003.htm DeckTech Premium Members Get Special Opportunity at Origins 2003!], swccgpc.com (12 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620164159/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/originspremium06122003.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

DeckTech's Premium Membership program began early in 2003. For about the price of a booster pack a month it offered members-only features and an exclusive discussion area, and premium members received a 20% discount off entry fees for all events co-sponsored by the Committee and DeckTech and were eligible for exclusive prizes; the DPC Championship at Origins 2003 was the first event where the discount applied. [[Neal Razi]] was the contact for the program.<ref name="pc-premium0612" /> At Origins 2003 the Committee took registrations for $15 premium memberships, and DeckTech donated $1 from each membership collected there to the Committee.<ref name="pc-premium0624">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/Events/2003/originspremium06242003.htm Decktech Offers Premium Memberships at Origins!], swccgpc.com (24 June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040620114821/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/Events/2003/originspremium06242003.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In November 2003 DeckTech was preparing its own sanctioning system, and [[Lee Edwards]] planned to run "Decktech sanctioned" tournaments "once that system is running".<ref name="pcf-2284-35301">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=35301#35301 Mass/NH tournaments], Lee Edwards, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 November 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040323101447/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=2284%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In May 2004 DeckTech announced a drawing among its premium members, including people who signed up for a premium membership, for one person to help design a new virtual card. Some players criticized it on the Players Committee forum, and [[Andrew Howard]] wrote that he had always been against random contests that let people design virtual cards.<ref name="pcf-3279-46070">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46070#46070 Decktech and V cards], deadbody, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (8 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-3279-46173">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46173#46173 Decktech and V cards], Andrew Howard, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> DeckTech had "about 70 or so" premium members at the time.<ref name="pcf-3279-46117">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46117#46117 Decktech and V cards], Rogue4, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (9 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> [[John Anderson]] said that [[Neal Razi]] could afford DeckTech's bandwidth only through premium memberships,<ref name="pcf-3279-46714">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46714#46714 Decktech and V cards], John Anderson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (24 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> and Lee Edwards said that $5 of every premium membership fee went to the Players Committee.<ref name="pcf-3279-46730">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730#46730 Decktech and V cards], Lee Edwards, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 May 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040625210908/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=46730%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

The Committee and DeckTech announced the North Carolina DeckTech Player's Challenge, held at Fallen Orc Games in Cary, North Carolina, on 22–24 October 2004, as the first Star Wars CCG World Qualifier of the new season; first and second place in its open-format event received byes into the [[2005 World Championship]].<ref name="pc-dpcnc04">[http://www.swccgpc.com/News/DPC%20Carolina%202004.htm North Carolina - DeckTech Player's Challenge - SWCCG Worlds Qualifier], swccgpc.com (2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041216042614/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/DPC%20Carolina%202004.htm Internet Archive]</ref>
